No actionable introduced defect was found. Reported macOS process-suite runs exercise the changed cleanup owner, but were not independently rerun; native Windows execution is explicitly deferred. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The ordinary contributor-proof gate is exempt for this MEMBER-authored PR. Reported macOS process-suite runs exercise the changed cleanup owner, but were not independently rerun; native Windows execution is explicitly deferred. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Current main still lacks group-disappearance confirmation: The main relay resolves extinction from a closing receipt without the added kernel process-group probe. Main’s only change since the pinned merge base is in diagnostics-prometheus, outside this PR’s introduced paths.
Latest-release comparison: The same receipt-only extinction path is present in v2026.9.2; the central repair is not already supplied by that release.
Independent result and cleanup settlement: The relay preserves an observed root result while drainage completes, and confirms POSIX extinction only after a closing receipt and ESRCH from a signal-zero group probe. Other probe failures retain uncertainty. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together OpenClaw’s process supervisor launches commands for agents, Gateway services, and the terminal interface. It returns command output and exit status while separately tracking whether owned processes have actually stopped. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Command caller] --> B[Process supervisor] B --> C[Child and process group] C --> D[Output and root result] C --> E[Cleanup owner] E --> F{Group disappearance confirmed?} F -->|Yes| G[Release cleanup ownership] F -->|No| H[Retain cleanup failure] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Commands requiring forced termination can leave shutdown reporting cleanup failure even after the root exits; the PR body explicitly accepts this operator-visible compatibility tradeoff. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P2)** - Native Windows process-start execution remains unverified; the supplied evidence covers its environment and timeout behavior with fixtures. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Retain the accepted cleanup contract (recommended)** Keep conservative shutdown failure reporting and the optional public helper additions as explicitly documented and accepted in the PR body. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the existing process owner as the single cleanup boundary, preserving command results and the maintainer-accepted conservative shutdown contract. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: pinned main accepts a closing receipt without checking group disappearance, and the regression cases cover descendants surviving root or descriptor closure. No runtime reproduction was executed in this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Extending the existing supervisor and native cleanup owner preserves the established result path while strengthening cleanup evidence; no competing implementation or persisted-data migration is introduced.
